$ai.role: You are an expert in the npm ecosystem, native Node.js addon build tooling, supply-chain security, and the structure of indicator-definitions.js in the npm/cli repository.
$ai.thisFileIs: A dataset generated by scripts/build-indicator-suggestions.js. It scans popular npm packages for lifecycle scripts and compares them against the INDICATOR_REGISTRY in lib/utils/indicator-definitions.js. Your job is to review the data below and propose concrete improvements to that file.
$ai.howToReadThisFile: The file is wrapped in an integrity envelope: { hash, data }. The actual content lives in the "data" field. Every section inside data (meta, coverage, existingDefinitionCoverage, uncategorizedPackages, lifecycleOnlyPackages, commandPatternGaps) has a "description" field that explains what the section contains and how to interpret it, and a "data" field with the actual content.  Read the description first, then inspect data.

tasks.task: Review commandPatternGaps.data where frequency >= 3 OR weeklyDownloadTotal >= 50000.
tasks.action: For each: decide whether the token warrants a NEW indicator entry (new build tool not yet covered) or just an additional commandPattern on an EXISTING entry.  Ignore tokens that are generic JS keywords (const, require, stdio, inherit) or non-build tools (tsc, oclif, lint, rimraf).

tasks.task: Review uncategorizedPackages.data sorted by weeklyDownloads descending.
tasks.action: For each: examine lifecycleScripts, commandTokens, detectedSignals, and inferredIndicatorFiles.  Propose a new INDICATOR_REGISTRY entry OR explain why it should not be added.  Focus on packages with weeklyDownloads > 10000.

tasks.task: Review existingDefinitionCoverage.data entries with low matchedCount.
tasks.action: Propose additional commandPatterns that would match real packages listed in the uncategorized or gap sections.

forNewIndicatorEntry.label: <short human-readable label>
commandPatterns: <regex source strings — will be compiled with new RegExp(...)>
forNewIndicatorEntry.addToNativeBuildCommandPattern: <true if this tool compiles native code>
forNewIndicatorEntry.rationale: <why this indicator is needed and what real packages triggered it>

native-build.description: Compiles a native binary (.node addon, .so, .dylib) via node-gyp, CMake, Meson, Autoconf, or similar

rust-native.description: Compiles a Rust-backed native addon (Cargo.toml / neon)

wasm-build.description: Compiles a WebAssembly (.wasm) module from Rust source (wasm-bindgen)

wasm-load.description: Loads a pre-compiled WebAssembly binary at runtime via WebAssembly.instantiate/compile — content is not inspectable by static analysis

gyp-conditions.description: binding.gyp has platform/arch conditions (may behave differently per OS)

make-build.description: Makefile or task-runner driven build (Grunt/Gulp/Jake/Cake/Rake/Brunch/Taskfile) that can execute arbitrary shell commands

binary-download.description: Downloads a pre-built binary at install time (node-pre-gyp, prebuild-install, etc.)

activates-bundled-binary.description: Makes a file bundled inside the npm tarball executable (chmod +x / fs.chmod with execute bit)

runtime-installer.description: Installs additional packages at runtime via npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/deno/bower install as a child process

external-url.description: Fetches a URL (curl/wget/node https) at install time

source-downloader.description: Fetches source code (curl/wget/git clone) at install time

dynamic-require.description: Calls require() with a non-literal argument — the loaded module cannot be statically determined

obfuscation-pattern.description: Uses Base64/hex decoding or eval/Function() to hide executed code

typescript-build.description: Compiles TypeScript source to JavaScript at prepare/install time (tsc, tsup, ts-node)

lint-check.description: Runs code quality and style checks at prepare/install time (ESLint, Prettier, etc.)

git-hook-setup.description: Installs or configures git hooks (husky, lefthook, simple-git-hooks) — hook scripts are scanned for build or network signals

platform-specific-install.description: Lifecycle script inspects process.platform / os.platform() to select or activate a platform-specific binary — different code paths run per OS/architecture

meta.description: Run metadata: when generated, registry size limit (topN), whether cross-package import following was enabled (deepScan), and the full indicator registry snapshot. registryDefinitions maps each indicator filename to its complete definition: label, detect (commandPatterns as {source,flags} objects, trigger flags), signals (onFound/onWarning), and scanner steps. See $ai.availableSignals for signal descriptions and the reverse mapping (signal → which indicators raise it).

steps.label: wasm-bindgen dependency (output is a .wasm module, not a native addon)
js-sys imported (direct JavaScript built-in access — includes eval, Function, Reflect)
wasm-bindgen-futures (async WASM ↔ JS bridge — spawns JS promises from Rust)
Contains C/C++ native code (externalNativeBuild — CMake or ndk-build)

native-build-command.label: Native build command in lifecycle script (no descriptor file)

steps.label: Contains C/C++ native code (externalNativeBuild — CMake or ndk-build)
External tools referenced in brunch config

coverage.description: Aggregate counts for this run. totalScanned = registry pages fetched. uniqueNamesConsidered = distinct package names seen. withLifecycleScripts = had install/postinstall/etc. matchedByExistingDefinitions = covered by at least one indicator. uncategorizedBuildPackages = build signal present but no indicator matched. lifecycleOnlyNoBuildHint = lifecycle scripts with no build tool detected.

existingDefinitionCoverage.description: Per-indicator match counts against real packages. Each entry is keyed by indicator filename with matchedCount and packages (sorted by weeklyDownloads desc). Each package entry includes name, version, weeklyDownloads, label, and signals. Deep mode: label+signals come from cached investigation results (scan-time registry). Non-deep mode: label+signals come from current registry definitions.
